```{r setup}
library(markerdata)
```

## Introduction

markerdata provides curated single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) marker
panels from public genomic resources, formatted as founder genotypes for
breeding-program simulation. Every panel is a plain data frame: five marker
metadata columns (`snp`, `allele`, `chr`, `pos`, `cm`) followed by one
genotype column per individual, coded `-1`/`0`/`1` (reference homozygote /
heterozygote / alternate homozygote).

One small maize panel (`SNP55K_maize282_maf04`) is bundled with the package
and loads instantly. Every other data set (crops, trees, cattle, sheep,
Atlantic salmon, and more; the catalog below lists them all) ships a sample
of 2,000 SNPs (1,000 for the four largest) for every individual that also loads instantly. For the
hosted panels, the whole panel is downloaded on first use with
`marker_data(name, full = TRUE)` and cached locally, so it does not bloat the
installed package. `Arabidopsis_div` (1001 Genomes) and `Human_div`
(1000 Genomes Project) are sample only: markerdata does not host their whole
data sets, and the `source_url` column of the catalog gives the original
download. The human data are from publicly released, consented 1000 Genomes
samples and are included for method development and teaching.

## The catalog

`marker_catalog()` lists every data set, with the size of the whole panel
(of the sample, for the two sample-only data sets),
and whether the whole panel is already available on this machine (bundled,
or already downloaded and cached):

```{r}
cat <- marker_catalog()
knitr::kable(cat[, c("name", "common_name", "n_snp", "n_ind", "het", "mating", "license")])
```

## The bundled data set

`SNP55K_maize282_maf04` is a maize marker matrix for the 282 inbred
association panel: 10,650 SNPs by 280 inbred lines.

```{r}
geno <- SNP55K_maize282_maf04
dim(geno)
head(geno[, 1:8])
```

The first five columns are marker metadata; the rest are one genotype
column per inbred line:

* `snp`: marker name.
* `allele`: allele pair, e.g. `"A/G"`.
* `chr`: chromosome, 1-10.
* `pos`: physical position in base pairs.
* `cm`: genetic position in centiMorgans.

Every genotype column holds a numeric (double) value in `{-1, 0, 1}`
(reference homozygote / heterozygote / alternate homozygote). The `cm`
column is a **synthetic** genetic map, generated from the physical
positions with `simplePHENOTYPES::synthetic_map()`; it is not taken from
any published maize linkage map, but it gives meiosis-based simulation
functions (crossing, selfing, doubled haploids) usable recombination
distances on this example data.

## Samples of the other panels

For every other data set, `marker_data()` returns the sample shipped with
the package. No download is needed:

```{r}
smp <- marker_data("Rice_div")
dim(smp)
```

A sample is a fixed thinning of the whole panel: every individual, and 2,000
SNPs (1,000 for `SoySNP50K_div`, `Cattle_div`, `Wheat_div` and `SugarBeet_div`, to keep the package small) evenly spaced over those that are polymorphic among them. It has the same columns and coding as the whole
panel. Use it for examples, tests and quick simulations, and the whole
panel for real studies. For `Arabidopsis_div` and `Human_div` the sample is
all that markerdata ships; `full = TRUE` warns, gives the `source_url` of the
original data and returns `NULL` without downloading anything:

```{r}
marker_catalog()[marker_catalog()$name %in% c("Arabidopsis_div", "Human_div"),
                 c("name", "n_snp", "n_ind", "source_url")]
```

## Polyploid crops

Two data sets come from polyploid crops, and the `-1`/`0`/`1` format cannot
hold allele dosage. `Potato_div` (autotetraploid) stores the source's dosages
0 to 4 as `-1` (dosage 0), `1` (dosage 4) and `0` (dosages 1 to 3), so about
69% of its calls are `0` and the dosage of the mixed genotypes is lost.
`Sugarcane_div` holds the diploid-style calls (`0/0`, `0/1`, `1/1`) that its
source reports, so it never had dosage, and its positions are *Sorghum
bicolor* coordinates. Read the help topics (`?Potato_div`, `?Sugarcane_div`)
before using them.

## Getting a whole panel

`full = TRUE` returns the whole panel. The first call downloads and caches
it, and later calls are served from the cache without any network access.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
geno <- marker_data("Rice_div", full = TRUE)
```

On first use, this downloads a small, packed file to `marker_cache_dir()`
(by default `tools::R_user_dir("markerdata", "cache")`, overridable with
`options(markerdata.cache = ...)` or the `MARKERDATA_CACHE` environment
variable), verifies it against a recorded checksum, and unpacks it into a
regular data frame. Subsequent calls with the same cache reuse the cached
file instantly. If the download fails (for example, no network connection),
`marker_data()` warns and returns `NULL` rather than raising an error.

Use `marker_download()` to fetch whole panels ahead of time, for example
before going offline. With no arguments it downloads every hosted panel (the sample-only data sets are skipped):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
marker_download(c("Rice_div", "Cattle_div"))
marker_download() # every whole panel
```

and `marker_cache_clear()` to remove cached files again:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
marker_cache_clear("Rice_div")
```

## Using the data with simplePHENOTYPES

Every marker data frame in this package is ready to use as founder
genotypes with `simplePHENOTYPES::as_population()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
geno <- marker_data("Cattle_div", full = TRUE)
pop <- simplePHENOTYPES::as_population(geno, individuals = 1:100)
```

## Citing the data

Cite the package itself with `citation("markerdata")`. Each data set keeps
its own original license and literature reference; get its citation with
`marker_references()`:

```{r}
marker_references("SNP55K_maize282_maf04")
print(marker_references("Rice_div"), style = "text")
```
